data.budget: read-only, no repository edits, about 40 tool calls
data.claim: Measured 2026-11-03: the topic tracks already cover about 14 stages, but (1) typed trace edges do not exist yet (ddflow link has only extends/duplicate_of/related/distinct; 5 shipped kinds have [[link]] fields; 0 requirement records), (2) eight-plus separate trace tasks (PD-trace owner, RQM-trace, US-trace, SPEC-trace, TF-trace, TM-matrix, RS-trace, CN-trace, SD-gaps) each plan their own view, (3) roles are defined in 8 places (GC-roles, B-sub-*, TM-roles, TF-roles, PD-roles, CN-roles, AI-roles, GV-workflows), (4) no per-project lifecycle profile, no stage-exit gate, no feedback intake from operation, no release-readiness gate. Smallest new set: 19 LF- integration tasks (profile, stage gates, one trace read model plus edge vocabulary, health, role catalogue and handoffs, e2e flow, feedback, docs sync, pm view, safety, multirepo, acceptance, docs). R-multirepo and R-change-mgmt were not filed when this ran.
data.falsifier: A topic track task already ships the lifecycle profile, a stage-exit gate or the cross-track trace read model (grep its body), or the sample project in LF-acceptance cannot go idea to feedback with only the records the tracks add plus the LF-* pieces
data.mechanism: event-log and queue inventory via ddflow task/phase/show, shipped kinds and gates read from the worktree, external practice fetched 2026-11-03; design reasoning for LF-*
data.probe:
ddflow phase list; ddflow task list --phase

data.question: Which integration pieces does ddflow need so one project runs the whole software cycle (discovery to feedback), given what the topic tracks already own?
